chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah al-Sayrafī from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding a person in iḥram who listened to a man having intercourse with his wife, and he ejaculated, he said: 'There is no penalty upon him.'
And there is no harm in a man kissing his mother, because that is from the aspect of mercy and affection, distinct from lust and natural inclination. It was narrated.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no penalty/obligation upon him
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of iḥram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person in ihram ejaculating after hearing intercourse, and is it permissible to kiss one's mother?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that auditory stimulation alone does not invalidate the iḥram state or incur a penalty for ejaculation, highlighting the distinction between mere hearing and visual or physical contact in fiqh. Furthermore, it legitimizes a man kissing his mother by categorizing the act as rooted in rahmah (mercy) and natural affection rather than shahwah (sexual lust), a nuance crucial for distinguishing it from marital intimacy.
